preamble: Fronting of a velar stop all the way to a palatalized dental [tʲ] is a rare outcome of velar palatalization; most languages stop at [c] or continue to [tʃ]. It is a defining innovation of the Southern New England Algonquian languages, where Proto-Eastern Algonquian *k became *ty /tʲ/ after *ē and some reflexes of Proto-Algonquian *i. Massachusett (Wampanoag) thus has wetu /wiːtʲəw/ 'house' where Abenakian and Unami languages keep the velar (wigwam, weekuwôm).

examples.note: The velar after the long front vowel became palatalized /tʲ/ (spelled ⟨ty⟩ in the modern orthography); the Abenakian/Unami cognate wigwam, weekuwôm retains k. The same innovation is shared by the other Southern New England Algonquian languages, so it counts as a single event.
Second-syllable *k became /tʲ/ after the long front vowel.
Palatalization before a schwa that continues an earlier *ī; /k/ is often restored by analogy before /aː/ and /əw/.
